sheet-52-1.description: The main map of sheet 52 shows the Seaside section of the Highlands of Navesink, today the borough of Highlands in Monmouth County, on the south shore of the Shrewsbury River. The catalog files the atlas under Ocean County, but the streets drawn here match Highlands. The river shoreline runs across the top of the sheet. Valley Avenue and Miller run down from the shore, and 3rd, 4th and 5th Streets cross between them. A short stretch of 6th Avenue leaves Miller to the east, and a street lettered Clam runs between Valley Avenue and Miller from the shore to 4th Street. Blocks 193 to 201 are drawn. Most of the buildings are small frame dwellings, many of them two-storey. Several stores stand on Miller near 3rd and 4th Streets, and one store has a cobbler's shop next to it. The institutions are the Dutch Reformed Church with its parsonage on Valley Avenue between 4th and 5th Streets, and the M.E. Church on Miller south of 3rd Street. A building east of Miller is lettered Derby Ho. A brook crosses block 199 from the west and runs into a stream that turns north along the east edge of the sheet to the river. South of 3rd Street there are ice ponds on both sides of Miller. Much of the ground is open and unbuilt, especially west of Valley Avenue and in block 199. The sheet is drawn at 60 feet to an inch with a compass rose at the lower right. Its lower left corner holds two insets, the Neptune Boat Club and a block on Navesink Avenue, and these are separate parts.
notes: Place: the Seaside section of Highlands borough, Monmouth County. The catalog record gives Ocean County.
Renamed: Valley Avenue is now Valley Street; 3rd Street is now Bay Avenue; 6th Avenue is now the first block of Shrewsbury Avenue east of Miller Street; Miller is Miller Street.
Clam (street) has no modern counterpart in OpenStreetMap.
5th Street is drawn only between Valley Avenue and Clam; it does not reach Miller as it does today. Valley Avenue ends at 4th Street on the sheet.
The stream along the east edge follows roughly the line of today's Shrewsbury Avenue south of the 6th Avenue block.

Seaside section of Highlands (Monmouth County, not Ocean County as catalogued), on the Shrewsbury River. Scale 60 ft to an inch. Three parts: part 1 main map (Valley Av, Clam, Miller, 3rd/4th/5th St, 6th Av); part 2 inset upper left of the lower-left corner: The Neptune Boat Club on the North Shrewsbury River (no streets, not placed); part 3 inset lower left: Navesink Av at Miller with school and Our Lady R.C. Church (anchored on one hand-picked junction). Renamings: 3rd St = Bay Avenue, 6th Av = Shrewsbury Avenue, Valley Av = Valley Street.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: The Neptune Boat Club, North Shrewsbury River (no street junction or other feature shared with the modern data or a placed sheet).

sheet-52-3.description: This inset in the lower left corner of sheet 52 shows a block on Navesink Avenue at Miller in the Highlands of Navesink, today the borough of Highlands in Monmouth County. It lies a short way south of the main map, close to where Miller Street meets today's Navesink Avenue (Route 36). The inset is drawn at the sheet's scale of 60 feet to an inch and at about the same orientation as the main map. Miller is lettered with a width of 60 feet and runs up the left edge of the inset. It is drawn with a small jog where it crosses Navesink Avenue, which is lettered with a width of 50 feet and runs across the inset from Miller to the right. North of the avenue is block 201, marked no exposure, with a school standing back from the street. South of the avenue is block 202. It holds Our Lady R.C. Church, 18 feet to the eaves, with a note giving 150 feet to the frame sheds, and four frame dwellings of one to three storeys. Lot numbers 101 to 112 run along both sides of the avenue. Much of the inset is open ground.
notes: Miller is today Miller Street. In OpenStreetMap its northern and southern stretches meet Navesink Avenue (NJ 36) about 32 m apart. The inset draws a jog of only about 4 m, so the control point uses the southern stretch, which lies on the old straight line of Miller Street.
Placed from one hand-picked junction with the scale and rotation of the main map: low confidence.
